Dear Dr. Mercer,

Thank you for evaluating this 14-year-old young man, whom I have been following for progressive skeletal and craniofacial issues that first became apparent around five years of age. He lives at home with his parents, attends mainstream eighth grade, and currently takes only daily multivitamin and vitamin D supplements.

His history is significant for repeated low-energy fractures of his extremities over the last nine years. Recent skeletal imaging reveals widespread demineralization across his entire skeleton, flattening of the thoracic vertebral bodies, and an evolving lateral spinal curvature. Cervical views showed focal malalignment with anterior slippage between the second and third cervical vertebrae, while his long bones demonstrate poor shaft remodeling with inadequate diaphyseal tapering. On musculoskeletal exam, he exhibits marked hyperextensibility of both knee joints, though his other peripheral joints are stable. His linear growth is severely restricted, leaving his height well below the third percentile.

His eyes display completely white sclerae with no blue discoloration. Notable facial features include an unusually bossed frontal region with heavy brow arches, an underdeveloped midface, a flattened bridge of the nose, and ears that project outward prominently. Oral examination revealed a restricted mouth opening, a steep, high-arched palate, and delayed emergence of his permanent teeth; however, the enamel appears sound, and there are no signs of opalescent dentin or dentinogenesis imperfecta. Audiometric evaluation recently identified a moderate bilateral sensorineural deficit. Cardiovascular, pulmonary, and abdominal examinations are entirely unremarkable.

I would greatly appreciate your assessment and guidance on how best to approach his continued care.

Sincerely,
Dr. Julian Wright
